fields.label: People, organizations & tools
fields.guidance: Name each contributor once. Credit their particular role in the relevant account, event or document. An authority reference describes identity; it does not authorize a person to act.

fields.label: Catalogue & external identifiers
fields.guidance: Record established identifiers and their issuing namespace. These references document identity; they do not verify an ownership or authority claim.

fields.label: Existing token references
fields.guidance: Identify an existing token and its relationship to this work. A supplied token reference does not bind this record to a contract or prove custody, title or creator authority.

fields.label: The form of the work
fields.guidance: Select every form that belongs to the artwork itself. A recording of an interview does not make a photograph a video work.

fields.label: Content & components
fields.guidance: Describe separately identifiable content, components and realizations of the work. Link received files without confusing the file with the work it carries.

fields.label: Physical objects
fields.guidance: Describe each print, proof, carrier or physical component individually. A description of delivery is an attributed account, not a museum custody receipt.

fields.label: Dimensions & measurements
fields.guidance: Record measurements against the relevant object. Image size and sheet size are separate measurements; include units and any uncertainty.

fields.label: Places
fields.guidance: Use the place name you want preserved in the public record. State whether it is a place of capture, a depicted place or another location. Museum staff can reconcile authority terms separately.

fields.label: Relationships
fields.guidance: Connect content, files, prints, documents and related works by their specific relationship. These connections retain distinctions that a list of filenames cannot.

fields.label: Related works & series
fields.guidance: Identify earlier versions, related works and series, including those without an online page.

fields.label: Inscriptions & marks
fields.guidance: Record text, signatures or marks that form part of the work or a specific physical object.

fields.label: Medium, technique & subject
fields.guidance: Retain your own wording for the work’s medium and technique. Authority references are attributed proposals until reconciled by the museum.

fields.label: Scale & duration
fields.guidance: Describe whether the work has fixed dimensions or duration, is variable, or is dimensionless. Measurements can be recorded separately for each component.

fields.label: Materials described but not deposited
fields.guidance: Keep a record of known material that has not been received. Name it accurately; this description does not create an upload or a preservation receipt.

fields.label: Full accounts & documents
fields.guidance: Preserve the complete account, with its paragraphs and headings. Identify authors and language; distinguish a reviewed text from a machine transcript or translation.

fields.label: Sources & references
fields.guidance: Cite books, notebooks, conversations and online resources. A source can be useful without a URL or an uploaded file.

fields.label: The history of the work
fields.guidance: Record events you know about, with their dates, people, places and evidence. Institutional accessions, legal title and custody are recorded separately by the responsible museum actor.

fields.label: Photography
fields.guidance: The circumstances of capture, the decisions that shaped the image, and the materials needed to preserve its appearance.

fields.label: Digital painting, illustration & collage
fields.guidance: Record the making of the image, its source projects, and how scale, color, texture and transparency should be carried forward.

fields.label: Video, animation & motion
fields.guidance: Describe time, motion and sound as experienced, alongside the master and the conditions needed for faithful playback.

fields.label: Audio, sound & music
fields.guidance: Describe the intended listening experience and retain the technical and creative choices that determine it.

fields.label: HTML & web
fields.guidance: Describe the complete web work, its point of entry and its behavior when networks, browsers or services change.

fields.label: Generative & software
fields.guidance: Identify what makes each realization a realization of this work: code, rules, inputs, randomness and the permitted range of change.

fields.label: Interactive work, games & participation
fields.guidance: Explain what a participant can do, how the work responds, and which interactions carry its meaning.

fields.label: 3D, spatial, AR & VR
fields.guidance: Describe scale, materials and spatial experience, including the devices and environment that make the work legible.

fields.label: Text, poetry & publications
fields.guidance: Retain the authoritative text and describe the relationship between language, typography, sequence and the space of reading.

fields.label: Installation, performance & mixed media
fields.guidance: Describe the work as a whole and the relationships among its components, site, hardware and individual realizations.

fields.label: Terms for supporting material
fields.guidance: Describe the rights that apply to each supporting contribution. The artwork release terms are fixed by the program when applicable; publication intent is not a claim of legal ownership.

fields.label: Presentation sequence
fields.guidance: Arrange the work in the order and space in which it should be encountered. Add timing, placement and accompanying text where they matter; leave technical values unset when they are not known.

fields.label: The work over time
fields.guidance: Describe the appearance, behavior and relationships that carry the work’s meaning. State what may change and why, with reference material where useful.

fields.label: Access to the work
fields.guidance: Describe captions, transcripts, alternative descriptions, controls and other provisions for encountering the work. Identify limits that are inherent to its form.

fields.label: Conversations about the work
fields.guidance: Preserve each complete conversation with its participants, questions, language and date. A written interview can stand on its own; name recordings only when they exist.

confirmation_copy: I have reviewed this version of the artwork record, including its accounts, credits, materials and uncertainty. The answers and selected files are intended for publication with the work. Museum enrichment remains separately attributed. Questions for the team are outside the artwork record. Confirmation records this version; it does not publish or mint the work.

prompts.text: What first drew you to make this work?
What is happening in the image, and what lies outside the frame that a future viewer should know?
Which choices in capture, construction or editing were most important to the final work?
How does this work relate to your practice and to other works in the same series?
What themes or ideas connect this work to the context in which it is being presented?
What is most likely to be misunderstood about this work?
What must remain intact when the work is displayed, reproduced or preserved?
Is there anything you would want someone encountering the work many years from now to know?
